attributes.title: Level 7

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓Did you place the sprite in the middle of the screen, on the “ground”?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where might the ninja sprite be placed on the screen?

❓ How might the scrolling background be used in this project?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 In this project, multiple animation assets will be created to set the ninja sprite to idle, fly, and walk in different directions. As a result, the scrolling background helps create the effect of the sprite actually moving the expected distance on screen.
steps.instructions:
Begin the project by adding a ninja sprite to the scene! 


Notice that the project already has code to set a scrolling background image and a tilemap. Notice there are also several ninja image assets in the Assets menu. 


Create a new sprite using the forwardNinja asset. Place the ninja sprite in the middle of the tilemap, on the “ground”. Code the sprite to move with direction buttons and set the camera to follow the sprite.


Click ▶ to see the sprite appear on screen.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the tools in the animation paint editor to show the person sprite bobbing up and down as they idle?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How might the marquee tool be used to make the person sprite appear shorter in the second frame? 

❓ When might the ninja sprite’s idle animation run?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 The ninja can use the marquee tool by clicking above the left side of the ninja image, then dragging their cursor to encompass the top half of the image and shifting it down by 1 or 2 pixels.
steps.instructions:
Create the ninja sprite’s idle animation using multiple frames!


In the Assets menu, open the forwardNinja asset. Use Ctrl + A to select, then copy the entire ninja image. Create an idleAnim animation asset, then paste the image into the first frame in the animation paint editor.


Duplicate the first frame in the idleAnim animation asset.


In the second frame, use the marquee tool to lower the sprite’s head to create a downward bobbing effect. Select the top half of the image, then shift it down by 1 or 2 pixels, covering the existing pixels, to make the sprite appear shorter.


Preview the animation on the upper right part of the screen, then make any adjustments to the frames as needed.

steps.hints: ❓Did you animate the ninja sprite with an idle animation?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What might the frame interval be set to so that the ninja sprite idles at a proper speed? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 As the ninja is tinkering with the runImageAnimation code, remind them to think about the value they used in the preview window of the animation paint editor. They may choose to use the same value, or run the image animation on screen, and choose a greater or lesser value based on the rate that the animation runs. 

💡 Prompt the ninja to use the documentation if they need help animating a sprite with an animation asset in their code.
steps.instructions:
Display the ninja sprite’s animation on screen!


Code the sprite to animate continuously using the idleAnim asset. 


Click ▶ to test the idle animation, then tinker with the frame interval value until the sprite is idling at a proper speed.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the paint tool to create walking movement in 3 frames?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where might the ninja’s feet be drawn in the second and third frames, so that they appear separate?

❓ How might pixels be rearranged so that the ninja sprite appears to “grow” in the third frame?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to consider how to draw the ninja’s feet so that they appear separate in the second and third frames. Encourage the ninja to use 2 different colors to show where each foot is in the image, before returning it back to black.
steps.instructions:
Create the ninja sprite’s walking right animation using multiple frames!


In the Assets menu, open the walkRight asset. Use Ctrl + A to select, then copy the entire ninja image. Create a walkRightAnim animation asset, then paste the image into the first frame in the animation paint editor. 


Notice how the legs appear to overlap in the first frame. Duplicate the first frame, then use the erase and draw tools in the second frame to draw the ninja’s right and left feet so they appear separate.  


Duplicate the second frame, then in the third frame, raise the top half of the image by 1 or 2 pixels to make the sprite appear taller. This frame will create the bobbing motion that naturally occurs when people walk. 


Preview the animation on the upper right part of the screen, then make any adjustments to the walking animation.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the horizontal flip tool to create a left facing sprite animation?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why does each frame need to be individually flipped in the walkLeftAnim animation asset?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that an animation asset consists of multiple pixel art still images. Because the animation cycles through each frame, each individual image must be horizontally flipped to reflect the new walking direction.
steps.instructions:
Create the left walking animation asset!


Duplicate the walkRightAnim animation asset, then rename the new asset walkLeftAnim. Use the horizontal flip tool to flip the image in each frame to create left facing sprite images.


Preview the animation on the upper right part of the screen to ensure each frame was flipped correctly.

steps.hints: ❓Did you add on button pressed events for right and  left buttons so that the sprite animation updates to the correct direction?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Which animation asset should be used in the right and  left button pressed events?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to double check that the animation asset direction matches the direction button pressed in the event.

💡 Prompt the ninja to use the documentation if they need help animating a sprite with an animation asset in their code.
steps.instructions:
Match the sprite’s animation to the direction that it’s walking. 


Return to the JavaScript editor and code the ninja sprite’s animation to change on right and left button pressed events. Update the runImageAnimation parameters accordingly.


Click ▶ to test the sprite animation when the direction buttons are pressed.

steps.hints: ❓Did you add an on anyButton released event so that the ninja sprite’s animation updates to idleAnim if it is not moving right or left?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why should the ninja sprite’s idle animation run when any button is released?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 The ninja sprite’s idle animation should run when any button is released, so that it shows that the sprite is not continuing to move in the same direction or making any other movements at the moment.

💡 Prompt the ninja to use the documentation if they need help animating a sprite with an animation asset in their code.
steps.instructions:
Oh no! The ninja sprite doesn’t face forward showing an idle animation anymore. 


Code the ninja sprite’s animation to change to idleAnim on an anyButton button released event. 


Click ▶ to test the sprite animation when the direction buttons are released.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the erase and paint tools to create realistic movement of the cape in the flyUpAnim animation asset?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where might pixels be added to create a cape behind the ninja?

❓ Where might pixels be added and erased to make the cape flow behind the ninja?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 As the ninja is tinkering with the animation frames, encourage them to think about what a cape’s movement might look like in real life. How might wind and air change its position? How might they connect pixels together to show this?
steps.instructions:
Create the ninja sprite’s jumping up animation using multiple frames!


In the Assets menu, open the upNinja asset. Use Ctrl + A to select, then copy the entire ninja image. Create a flyUpAnim animation asset, then paste the image into the first frame in the animation paint editor.


Duplicate the first frame in the flyUpAnim animation asset two times. 


In each frame, use the paint and erase tools to add a flowing cape behind the ninja, making the cape image look slightly different than the frame before. 


Consider how a cape might move in real life as the ninja flies up; showing where it might flutter up and down and how wind and air might cause the cape’s outline to shift in unpredictable and random ways.  


Preview the animation on the upper right part of the screen, then make any adjustments to the flying animation.

steps.hints: ❓Did you update the ninja sprite’s ay property to 0 whenever the up button is pressed?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why should the ninja sprite be assigned a positive y-acceleration value at the beginning of the project?

❓ What happens when the up button is pressed?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 The ninja sprite should be assigned a positive y-acceleration value at the beginning of the project so that gravity is created and triggers the idle animation to run.

💡 When the up button is pressed, the ninja sprite’s y-acceleration is set back to 0 while the flyUpAnim runs, so that the ninja sprite can remain in the air while “flying”.
steps.instructions:
Match the sprite’s animation to the direction that it’s flying.


Code the ninja sprite’s animation to change to the flyUpAnim animation asset on an up button pressed event.


Find the code that creates the ninja sprite, then assign the sprite a positive ay value, creating gravity at the start of the project.


Inside the up button pressed event, set the ninja sprite’s y-acceleration to 0 so that the ninja sprite doesn’t fall back to the ground when it’s flying. 


Click ▶ to test the ninja sprite’s animation when the up button is pressed.

steps.hints: ❓Did you update the direction parameter to Bottom in isHittingTile function?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why is it necessary to check if the bottom of a sprite is hitting a wall tile, when the left and right buttons are pressed, and when any button is released?

❓ What happens when the left and right buttons are pressed while the ninja sprite is flying?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that tilemaps can be useful in a project, even if there are not visible tiles on screen. In this example, transparent wall tiles are placed along the bottom of the screen. Because of this, the program is able to detect whether the ninja is standing on the ground, or flying in the air, in order to control game conditions.


💡 If the ninja is flying when the left and right buttons are pressed, only the ninja’s up animation will show.
steps.instructions:
Oh no! The ninja sprite idles in mid air without a cape. 


In the Assets menu, open the groundTilemap and notice that there is a row of blank wall tiles on the bottom row. 


Inside the right and left button pressed events, add a conditional that will only run the animation code if the bottom of the ninja sprite is hitting a wall tile. 


Add the same conditional inside the anyButton released event so that the ninja sprite only idles if it’s on the ground. 


Click ▶ to test the ninja sprite’s animation when the sprite is on the ground and when it is flying.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the paint and erase tools to make the cape flutter realistically, as a flag might wave in the wind?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What might change in each frame to create a flying animation for the ninja sprite?

❓ Where might pixels be added or removed to show the cape flying in the wind?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 As the ninja is tinkering with the animation frames, encourage them to think about what a cape’s movement might look like in real life from the side. How might wind and air change its position? How might they connect pixels together to show this?
steps.instructions:
Create the ninja sprite’s flying right animation using multiple frames!


In the Assets menu, open the flyRightNinja asset. Use Ctrl + A to select, then copy the entire ninja image. Create a flyRightAnim animation asset, then paste the image into the first frame in the animation paint editor.


Duplicate the first frame in the flyRightAnim animation asset two times.


In each new frame, use the erase and paint tools to make the cape image look slightly different than the one before. 


Consider how a cape might move in real life as the ninja flies to the side; showing where it might flutter up and down and how wind and air might cause the cape’s outline to shift in unpredictable and random ways.  


Preview the animation on the upper right part of the screen, then make any adjustments to the flying right animation.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the horizontal flip tool to create a left facing sprite animation?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why does each frame need to be individually flipped in the flyLeftAnim animation asset?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that an animation asset consists of multiple pixel art still images. Because the animation cycles through each frame, each individual image must be horizontally flipped to reflect the new flying direction.
steps.instructions:
Create the left flying animation asset!


Duplicate the flyRightAnim animation asset, then rename the new asset flyLeftAnim. Use the horizontal flip tool to flip the sprite image in each frame to create left facing sprite images.


Preview the animation on the upper right part of the screen to ensure each frame was flipped correctly.

steps.hints: ❓Did you update the parameters to the correct flying animation asset names?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ When will the ninja sprite’s flying up animation show? When will its walking animation show?

❓ What might the frame interval be set to so that the ninja sprite idles at a proper speed? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 When the left or right buttons are pressed, if the bottom of the ninja sprite is touching a wall tile, then the sprite’s walking animation will run. If it is not touching a wall tile (and is flying in the air), then the sprite’s flying animation will run.

💡 As the ninja is tinkering with the runImageAnimation code, remind them to think about the value they used in the preview window of the animation paint editor. They may choose to use the same value, or run the image animation on screen, and choose a greater or lesser value based on the rate that the animation runs. 

💡 Prompt the ninja to use the documentation if they need help animating a sprite with an animation asset in their code.
steps.instructions:
Match the sprite’s animation to the direction that it’s flying. 


Inside the right and left button pressed events, add an else condition that sets the animation to the flying animation assets when the ninja sprite is not hitting a wall tile on the bottom of the sprite. Update the runImageAnimation parameters accordingly. 


Click ▶ to test the ninja sprite’s animation when the direction buttons are pressed and the sprite is flying.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the erase and paint tools to create realistic movement of the cape in the flyDownAnim animation asset?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What might change in each frame to create an animation for the ninja sprite flying down?

❓ Where might pixels be added or removed to show the cape flying in the wind?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 As the ninja is tinkering with the animation frames, encourage them to think about what a cape’s movement might look like in real life from the side. How might wind and air change its position? How might they connect pixels together to show this?
steps.instructions:
Create the ninja sprite’s flying down animation using multiple frames!


In the Assets menu, open the flyDownNinja asset. Use Ctrl + A to select, then copy the entire ninja image. Create a flyDownAnim animation asset, then paste the image into the first frame in the animation paint editor.


Duplicate the first frame in the flyDownAnim animation asset two times.


In each new frame, use the erase and draw tools to make the cape image look slightly different than the one before. 


Consider how a cape might move in real life as a ninja flies down; showing where it might flutter up and down and how wind and air might cause the cape’s outline to shift in unpredictable and random ways. 


Preview the animation on the upper right part of the screen, then make any adjustments to the flying down animation.

steps.hints: ❓What symbol can be used to check if a condition is not true?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What will happen when the down button is pressed?

❓ Why is the ninja sprite’s y-acceleration set to 500 when the down button is pressed?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to use the documentation if they need help using a NOT operator in the conditional.

💡 When the down button is pressed, if the bottom of the sprite is not touching a wall tile (meaning it’s flying in the air), the flying down animation will run and the ninja sprite’s y-acceleration will be set to 500.

💡 The ninja sprite’s y-acceleration will be set to 500 to create gravity to cause the sprite to fall back down to the ground.
steps.instructions:
Update the ninja sprite’s animation as it flies down! 


Code the ninja sprite’s animation to change on down button pressed events. Add a conditional that will only run the animation code if the ninja sprite is not hitting a wall tile on the bottom of the sprite. 


Inside the conditional, reset the ay property to a positive value so that the sprite falls to the ground. 


Click ▶ to test the ninja sprite’s animation when the down button is pressed.

steps.hints: ❓Did you update the sprite parameter in the stopAnimation function?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why should all image animation stop when the down button is released?

❓ What happens now when the down button is released?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 When the down button is released, the ninja sprite will fall back down to the ground and the flying down animation will stop. The ninja sprite’s image will be set to the forwardNinja asset. Once standing on the ground, the ninja sprite’s idle animation will run.
steps.instructions:
Oh no! The ninja sprite continues to look like it’s flying down even after it’s touched the floor. 


Code the sprite animation to stop and reset to the forwardNinja image asset when the down button is released. 


Click ▶ to test the ninja sprite’s animation when the down button is released.

steps.hints: ❓Did you tinker with all the runImageAnimation functions and notice how the animation changes depending on the parameters?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What do you notice about each type of movement animation?

❓ How are the animations similar? How are they different?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to look across the animations that run when the ninja sprite is moving in different ways and notice what looks similar and what looks different. Have the ninja consider the speed of the animations, the direction that the animations are moving the sprite in, and how the animations are affecting each sprite’s movement.
steps.instructions:
Compare the different types of animations on the ninja sprite!


Move the ninja sprite in different directions and notice how the animation changes depending on whether the ninja sprite is touching the floor or flying in the air. Tinker with the frame intervals and compare how the animations are similar and different!

subgroups.introduction: Animate a superhero ninja as it walks and flies in different directions!

validationItems.text: Create custom animation and image sprites for us in the project.
Use an idleAnim asset with at least 2 frames to animate the sprite when standing still.
Use walkLeftAnim, walkRightAnim, flyLeftAnim, and flyRightAnim assets to animate the sprite’s left and right walking and flying movement. Use at least 3 frames in each animation asset.
Use flyUpAnim and flyDownAnim assets with at least 3 frames each to animate the sprite’s flying up and down movement.
Change the sprite animation when the sprite is moving left or right, depending on whether the sprite is flying or walking.
Change to the idle animation when any button is released and the sprite is hitting a wall tile on the bottom.
Reset the sprite's image when the down button is released.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 7 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about using still images to create animation assets. Different frames can be combined in the animation paint editor to animate a sprite’s movement in many different ways. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 7:

badges.title: I Like to Move It, Move It
badges.description: Use a variety of animation techniques to add movement to pixel art images in a project.

badges.title: Take it for a Spin
badges.description: Create animation assets that give the illusion of a sprite rotating or spinning.

badges.title: Boing!
badges.description: Create animation assets using squash and stretch that give the illusion of a sprite bouncing.

badges.title: Loafin’ Around
badges.description: Create an idle animation for a sprite.

badges.title: Frame by Frame
badges.description: Create animation assets that mimic the realistic movement of objects.

badges.title: It’s Alive!
badges.description: Use different layers to display an animation asset between 2 image assets.
